candidates.label: prepTime
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the duration required to prepare items for use in instructions or a direction. Also called preparation duration, setup time, readiness time. Examples: A recipe has a prep time of 'PT15M'. A DIY project has a prep time of 'PT30M'. A cooking instruction has a prep time of 'PT10M'. Distinct from performTime, which is the time to execute the instructions.

candidates.label: jobImmediateStart
candidates.comment: An employment timing relation indicating whether a job position is available for an immediate start. Also called immediate start, urgent hire, start now, ready to begin. Examples: A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'true'. A job posting has jobImmediateStart set to 'false'. This position has jobImmediateStart as 'true' for qualified candidates. Distinct from jobStartDate, which specifies a particular date.

candidates.label: expectsAcceptanceOf
candidates.comment: An expects acceptance of relation between an action access specification, consume action, or media subscription and an offer that must be accepted before the action can be performed. Also called: requires offer, prerequisite offer, conditional offer. Examples: "Watch Movie Action" expects acceptance of "Movie Purchase Offer", "Download Software Action" expects acceptance of "Software License Offer", "Access Premium Content" expects acceptance of "Subscription Offer".

candidates.label: exercisePlan
candidates.comment: An exercise plan relation between an exercise action and the specific plan or routine followed during the action. Also called: workout routine, training regimen, fitness program. Examples: "Morning Run" exercise plan "Couch to 5K Plan", "Weightlifting Session" exercise plan "StrongLifts 5x5", "Yoga Practice" exercise plan "Beginner Vinyasa Flow".

candidates.label: possibleTreatment
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: primaryPrevention
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a preventative therapy used to avert the initial occurrence of a medical condition. Also called preventative measure, initial prevention, prophylactic therapy. Examples: A medical condition has a primary prevention of 'vaccination'. Heart disease has a primary prevention of 'healthy diet'. Infection has a primary prevention of 'hand washing'.

candidates.label: riskFactor
candidates.comment: A factor that increases the likelihood of a patient developing a specific medical condition. Also called predisposing factor, risk element, vulnerability factor. Examples: `Heart Disease` riskFactor `High Cholesterol`, `Diabetes` riskFactor `Obesity`, `Lung Cancer` riskFactor `Smoking`.

chosen_property.label: drivenByExperienceWith
chosen_property.definition: Was motivated or influenced by experience with something.

candidates.label: experienceInPlaceOfEducation
candidates.comment: An experience in place of education relation indicating whether a job posting accepts relevant experience as an alternative to formal educational qualifications. Also called: experience substitutes education, education equivalency, alternative qualification. Examples: "Senior Developer Job" experience in place of education "true", "Entry-Level Marketing Position" experience in place of education "false", "Project Manager Role" experience in place of education "true".

candidates.label: hasDriveThroughService
candidates.comment: A drive-through service availability relation for a place, indicating whether it offers services accessible by driving through. Also called offers drive-through, drive-through available, drive-in service. Examples: "A restaurant has drive-through service.", "A testing facility has drive-through service.", "The bank has drive-through service for transactions."

candidates.label: experienceRequirements
candidates.comment: An experience requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the necessary skills and experience for the role. Also called: required experience, skill requirements, professional background. Examples: "Software Engineer Job" experience requirements "5+ years in Java development", "Marketing Manager Occupation" experience requirements "Proven track record in digital marketing campaigns", "Chef Position" experience requirements "Culinary school degree and 3 years restaurant experience".

candidates.label: monthsOfExperience
candidates.comment: A required number of months of experience for an occupational role. Also called experience duration, minimum experience, required experience in months. Examples: "Software Engineer Role monthsOfExperience 24", "Marketing Manager Position monthsOfExperience 60", "Entry-level Job monthsOfExperience 0".

candidates.label: driveWheelConfiguration
candidates.comment: A drive wheel configuration relation between a vehicle and the value or text describing which roadwheels receive torque from the engine. Also called "drivetrain type", "wheel drive system". Examples: "Car 'SUV' driveWheelConfiguration 'AllWheelDriveConfiguration'", "Truck driveWheelConfiguration '4x4'", "Sedan driveWheelConfiguration 'FrontWheelDriveConfiguration'".

candidates.label: steeringPosition
candidates.comment: A specification of the steering wheel's position in a vehicle, typically for cars. Also called "steering wheel side", "driver's side", "left-hand drive", "right-hand drive". Examples: "The car has steeringPosition LeftHandDriving", "This vehicle's steeringPosition is RightHandDriving", "The steeringPosition indicates where the driver sits."

candidates.label: vehicleSpecialUsage
candidates.comment: A vehicle special usage relation between a vehicle and an indication of whether it has been used for special purposes like commercial rental or as a taxi. Also called special use, commercial use, past usage. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Taxi'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Commercial Rental'", "Vehicle vehicleSpecialUsage 'Driving School'".

candidates.label: affectedBy
candidates.comment: An affected by relation between a medical test and the drugs that can influence its results. Also called influenced by, impacted by, drug interaction. Examples: "A blood test's results are affected by 'anticoagulants'.", "The diagnostic test is affected by 'caffeine'."

candidates.label: speed
candidates.comment: A quantitative value representing the speed range of a vehicle. Also called "vehicle speed", "maximum speed", "speed capability", "velocity range". Examples: "The car has speed 200 KMH", "The boat's speed is 30 knots", "This vehicle's speed range is 0-120 mph."

candidates.label: vehicleInteriorType
candidates.comment: A vehicle interior type relation between a vehicle and the type or material of its interior. Also called interior material, upholstery type, cabin trim. Examples: "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'leather'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'synthetic fabric'", "Vehicle vehicleInteriorType 'wood trim'".

chosen_property.label: willSeek
chosen_property.definition: Intends to look for or pursue something or someone.

candidates.label: seeks
candidates.comment: A demand for specific products or services expressed by an organization or person. Also called desires, looks for, requests, requires. Examples: `Company X` seeks `Demand for Software Developers`, `Person Y` seeks `Demand for Used Car`, `Organization Z` seeks `Demand for Consulting Services`. Distinct from `offers`, which is about what is provided.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: targetCollection
candidates.comment: A specific collection relation between an update action and the collection of things that is the target of the action. Also called "collection to update", "target set", "destination collection". Examples: "The add action has targetCollection a list of items", "The update action's targetCollection is a database table", "This action modifies a targetCollection of documents.". Distinct from object, which is a more general target of an action.

candidates.label: expectsAcceptanceOf
candidates.comment: An expects acceptance of relation between an action access specification, consume action, or media subscription and an offer that must be accepted before the action can be performed. Also called: requires offer, prerequisite offer, conditional offer. Examples: "Watch Movie Action" expects acceptance of "Movie Purchase Offer", "Download Software Action" expects acceptance of "Software License Offer", "Access Premium Content" expects acceptance of "Subscription Offer".

candidates.label: possibleTreatment
candidates.comment: A medical attribute indicating a potential treatment, drug, or therapy to address a medical condition, sign, or symptom. Also called potential therapy, recommended treatment, intervention option. Examples: A medical condition has a possible treatment of 'antibiotics'. A symptom has a possible treatment of 'pain relievers'. Hypertension has a possible treatment of 'lifestyle modification'.

candidates.label: eligibleCustomerType
candidates.comment: An eligible customer type relation between a demand or offer and the business entity type for which it is valid. Also called "customer segment", "target customer", "valid for". Examples: "Offer 'Student Discount' eligibleCustomerType 'Student'", "Demand 'Wholesale Order' eligibleCustomerType 'Business'", "Offer 'Senior Citizen Rate' eligibleCustomerType 'Senior'".

candidates.label: quest
candidates.comment: A quest relation between a game or video game series and a specific task or mission that players can complete for a reward. Also called mission, task, objective. Examples: "A role-playing game features a quest to 'defeat the dragon'.", "A video game series includes a quest to 'collect all artifacts'.", "An adventure game has a quest to 'rescue the princess'."

candidates.label: offeredBy
candidates.comment: An organization or person making an offer. Also called provided by, seller, vendor, offered from. Examples: "Product Offer offeredBy 'Acme Corp'", "Service Offer offeredBy 'John Doe'", "Event Ticket Offer offeredBy 'Ticketmaster'". Distinct from seller, which is a more specific term for a person or organization selling something.

candidates.label: offers
candidates.comment: An offer or demand related to a product, service, event, or other item. Also called available offers, related offers, product offers. Examples: "Product X offers 'Offer to sell'", "Service Y offers 'Demand for service'", "Event Z offers 'Offer for tickets'". Distinct from hasOfferCatalog, which points to a catalog of offers.

candidates.label: potentialAction
candidates.comment: A behavioral attribute indicating an idealized action in which a thing could potentially serve as the object. Also called possible action, available action, actionable item. Examples: A product has a potential action 'BuyAction'. A book has a potential action 'ReadAction'. A movie has a potential action 'WatchAction'.
